original: Recent analysis also indicates that the city's freshwater sources became highly contaminated with mercury, phosphate and cyanobacteria leading to the accumulation of toxins. Tikal and its immediate surroundings seem to have lost most of their population between 830 and 950 and central authority
sampled:
collapsed. However, the exact causes of the collapse of the Mayan civilization are still debated.

In the early 1980s, it was theorized that, in addition to the collapse of the ancient Mayan society, the collapse of the Maya was related to the decline of the Great Maya Aquifer (GMA), a large underground freshwater system of the Yucatán Peninsula. This scenario was based on the combination of archaeological evidence from the Maya city of Tikal and geochemical analyses.

A number of sites in nearby areas of the Yucatán Peninsula are also under threat from groundwater extraction.

The Great Maya Aquifer
The Great Maya Aquifer is a very large aquifer system located in the Yucatán Peninsula. It is the largest underground freshwater system in the world, and is estimated to cover 7,000 km².

The GMA runs from the Sierra Madre Occidental in the east to the Gulf of Mexico in the west.
